name: poulami95/market-triangulation
method: Monte Carlo triangulating order-book guidance, Hyperliquid pre-IPO perp and Polymarket brackets; Python stdlib
thesis: ANT prices above its $70-$78 range and opens near where offshore money already trades it. The book is ~6.9x covered and it guided to the top of the range or above (Bloomberg, 17 Nov) and now plans to raise the price (WSJ, 18 Nov), so the model puts 84% on a price above $78 and a median of $82.86, capped where banks would still leave ~8% headroom under the Hyperliquid xyz:ANT perp ($96.61). The open blends that perp, discounted for its offshore retail premium (it has fallen from $138 at listing), with a SpaceX-style pop on the simulated IPO price: median $95.37. The close is simulated from 6 comparable mega-IPO open-to-close moves, then tilted toward Polymarket's first-day market-cap brackets (33% <$1.25T, 39% $1.25T-1.5T, 27% $1.5T+); median $96.70. Day 5 adds comps' drift, a drag for the up-to-316M-share first-day lock-up release, and greenshoe support below issue: median $94.21. With a 6.3% float and a 20% retail slice, volatility is scaled by VIX (18.7) and ranges are widened 15% because pre-trade markets are under-dispersed. Signal pack not present (licensed, gitignored, sent to registrants); tilt = 0.
key_risks: Up to 316M existing shares can sell on day one, about 38% of the offering, which could cap the close and day 5
The xyz:ANT perp is an offshore crypto derivative with no claim on shares; its premium has been volatile ($138 to ~$97) and may not converge to the Nasdaq open
A 6.3% float with a 20% retail allocation makes the first days prone to squeezes or sharp fades beyond comparable IPOs
Nvidia beat on 17 Nov but most of its 4.8% after-hours jump faded overnight; a weak AI tape on 19 Nov would hit the open
An upsized deal or an early greenshoe exercise adds supply and lowers the pop for any given IPO price

extra_predictions.statement: ANT closes the fifth trading day below its IPO price
